hook_text: A squashed sandwich and a leaking shop roof were fixed with the same five steps. Here they are.
clip_script: Thabo's sandwiches get flattened by his textbooks. Mrs Dlamini's shop roof drips onto the maize meal. Different problems, same method. I: investigate. Thabo measures his bag; she finds the rusty nail hole. D: design. He sketches a box, a sleeve and a biscuit tin; she weighs a new sheet against a cheap patch. M: make. He lines the tin; she screws the patch on and seals it. E: evaluate. His tin rattles, so back to design for a pad; her roof shows more rust, so back to investigate. C: communicate. He shows the class his sketches; she tells her neighbour. Investigate, design, make, evaluate, communicate. IDMEC. It is a loop, not a line, and it is exactly how you will build a working rescue device this term.
visual_style: Whiteboard circle of five letters; a sandwich tin and a tin roof patch orbit it, with arrows looping back from E to D and from E to I.
mood: Friendly and brisk, everyday problems made orderly.
pacing: Two problems set up in five seconds, then one beat per letter, ending on the loop.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort one problem of your own into the five steps.
